seo.title: Best Wine Bars in Amman (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover Amman's top wine bars, from cozy hideaways to vibrant rooftops. Explore the finest selections of local and international wines, paired with delicious food, across the city's best neighborhoods.

hero.subtitle: Amman's wine scene offers an enticing blend of sophisticated lounges, lively bistro bars, and hidden gems where you can savor excellent local and international vintages.

picks.name: Canvas Bistro
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Canvas Bistro is renowned for its sophisticated ambiance and an impressive, curated wine list featuring international and local labels. It's an ideal spot for a romantic evening or a refined gathering, offering impeccable service and delicious bistro-style dishes that perfectly complement their wines.
picks.whatToOrder: A bottle from their 'Hidden Gems' selection, paired with their delectable Beef Carpaccio.
picks.insiderTip: Make a reservation, especially on weekends, as it's a popular spot. Inquire about their seasonal wine-tasting events.
picks.redditQuote: "Canvas Bistro truly feels like a little piece of Europe in Amman. Their sommelier was incredibly helpful, and the ambiance is just perfect for a date night. Definitely worth the price for the selection!"

picks.name: The Loft
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Perched atop a building in Abdoun, The Loft offers a chic, vibrant atmosphere with stunning city views, making it a fantastic spot for sunset drinks. While also known for cocktails, their wine selection is thoughtfully chosen, covering a good range of international reds, whites, and sparkling wines.
picks.whatToOrder: A glass of crisp Sauvignon Blanc while enjoying the city lights.
picks.insiderTip: Arrive early to snag a good spot on the terrace, especially during peak season. Their happy hour deals are fantastic value.
picks.redditQuote: "The views from The Loft are unmatched in Amman. Great place to unwind with friends, and their wine list, though not huge, has some solid choices. Good vibe all around!"

picks.name: Maestro Restaurant & Bar
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Maestro is a beloved spot on Rainbow Street, celebrated for its live music, lively atmosphere, and warm, rustic charm. They offer a respectable wine list with a focus on approachable local and international wines, perfect for enjoying alongside their delicious Mediterranean small plates and lively performances.
picks.whatToOrder: A glass of Jordanian St. George Red and their Mixed Mezza Platter.
picks.insiderTip: Check their schedule for live music nights; it can get quite busy and vibrant. Seating near the stage fills up quickly.
picks.redditQuote: "Maestro's is always a good time, especially with the live bands. Not a huge wine snob selection, but they have decent options to sip on while enjoying the music and people-watching. So much fun!"

picks.name: Blue Fig Cafe & Jazz Club
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A long-standing Amman favorite, Blue Fig offers a unique blend of a cozy cafe, upscale restaurant, and a vibrant jazz club. Their extensive menu includes a well-curated wine list featuring labels from around the world, making it a versatile spot for a casual drink, dinner, or a sophisticated night out.
picks.whatToOrder: A bottle of New World Pinot Noir with their signature Lamb Chops.
picks.insiderTip: They often have themed nights or special events, so check their social media. The outdoor terrace is lovely in good weather.
picks.redditQuote: "Blue Fig is my go-to for a relaxed evening with friends. The wine list is surprisingly good, and their food never disappoints. Plus, you might catch some great live jazz!"

picks.name: Fakhreldin Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While primarily a high-end Lebanese restaurant, Fakhreldin boasts an elegant bar area and a wine list that could rival many dedicated wine establishments. It's the perfect place to enjoy premium Lebanese cuisine with an expertly paired wine from their extensive collection, all within a beautiful, traditional setting.
picks.whatToOrder: A premium Lebanese wine like Chateau Ksara Reserve du Couvent with a selection of hot and cold Mezze.
picks.insiderTip: Beyond the dining room, their bar area offers a more intimate setting for just drinks. Dress code is smart casual.
picks.redditQuote: "Fakhreldin is exceptional. I didn't expect such a stellar wine list at a Lebanese place, but they truly deliver. The service is impeccable, and the experience feels very luxurious."

picks.name: Cucina (InterContinental Amman)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located within the InterContinental Hotel, Cucina offers an authentic Italian dining experience with a strong emphasis on wine. Their cellar houses an impressive selection of Italian and international wines, perfectly chosen to complement their classic pasta, pizza, and regional dishes. It's a sophisticated spot for discerning palates.
picks.whatToOrder: A Super Tuscan or a bold Barolo with their homemade Tagliatelle al Ragù.
picks.insiderTip: They often have wine pairing dinners or special promotions; check with the hotel concierge. The atmosphere is quiet and refined.
picks.redditQuote: "Cucina at the Intercontinental is surprisingly good for wine. Their Italian reds are fantastic, and the staff are quite knowledgeable about pairings. A great escape from the busy city."

picks.name: District Urban Brewery
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While primarily known for its craft beer, District Urban Brewery also boasts a surprisingly solid wine list, catering to those who prefer grapes over hops. It has a relaxed, industrial-chic vibe, making it a great place to unwind with friends over a good glass of wine and some elevated pub fare.
picks.whatToOrder: A robust Cabernet Sauvignon with their gourmet burgers or sliders.
picks.insiderTip: The outdoor seating area is popular in cooler months. They have a good happy hour for both beer and wine options.
picks.redditQuote: "Even if you're not a beer person, District has a decent wine selection. It's a great casual spot with a cool atmosphere to hang out and have a few drinks. Plus, the food is surprisingly good!"

picks.name: Books@Cafe
picks.whyItMadeTheList: More than just a cafe, Books@Cafe is a cultural landmark on Rainbow Street, offering a unique blend of books, food, and drinks, including a modest but well-chosen wine list. It's perfect for a relaxed afternoon sip or an informal evening gathering, offering stunning views from its terrace.
picks.whatToOrder: A light Chardonnay or local white wine, enjoyed with a good book or the sunset views.
picks.insiderTip: Grab a table on the terrace for the best views, especially around sunset. It's also a great spot for people-watching on Rainbow Street.
picks.redditQuote: "Books@Cafe is such a chill spot. You can grab a book, order a glass of wine, and just relax. It's not fancy, but the vibe and the views are unmatched for the price. Love it!"

picks.name: Copas
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Copas brings a vibrant slice of Spain to Amman, specializing in delicious tapas and an excellent selection of Spanish wines, including Cava and Rioja. The lively atmosphere and shared plates make it an ideal venue for groups looking to enjoy good wine, food, and conversation.
picks.whatToOrder: A bottle of robust Rioja Reserva paired with their Patatas Bravas and Gambas al Ajillo.
picks.insiderTip: They often have themed Spanish nights or live music, which can add to the festive atmosphere. Reservations are recommended on weekends.
picks.redditQuote: "Copas is my favorite for a fun night out. Their Spanish wines are fantastic, and the tapas are so authentic. It's always buzzing with energy, great for groups!"

picks.name: Wild Jordan Center Rooftop
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Offering one of Amman's most iconic views overlooking the Citadel and old city, the Wild Jordan Center's rooftop cafe provides a serene setting to enjoy local food and a decent wine selection. It's less of a dedicated wine bar and more of a unique cultural experience with the option to enjoy a good glass of wine.
picks.whatToOrder: A glass of local wine (red or white) with the traditional Saj bread and dips, soaking in the panoramic views.
picks.insiderTip: Visit just before sunset for breathtaking views. It's a great spot for tourists looking for a unique Amman experience with a drink.
picks.redditQuote: "The Wild Jordan Center views are insane, and being able to sip on a glass of wine while watching the sunset over the Citadel is pure magic. Not a huge wine selection, but enough to enjoy the moment."

picks.name: Whispers Lounge & Bar (The St. Regis Amman)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: For an unparalleled luxury experience, Whispers Lounge at The St. Regis Amman offers an opulent setting and an exquisitely curated wine and spirits list. It's an intimate, sophisticated space perfect for discerning guests seeking high-end vintages, premium service, and a tranquil atmosphere away from the city's bustle.
picks.whatToOrder: A glass from their premium reserve wine list, paired with an artisanal cheese board.
picks.insiderTip: Dress smart casual. This is more of a quiet, exclusive lounge than a lively bar, ideal for a discreet conversation or a business meeting.
picks.redditQuote: "Whispers at St. Regis is definitely a splurge, but if you want top-tier wine and incredible service in a super elegant setting, this is it. Felt like royalty sipping a Barolo there."

picks.name: Trader Vic's Amman
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While famous for its exotic cocktails, Trader Vic's also offers a solid wine list, making it a unique spot to enjoy a glass in a vibrant, Polynesian-themed setting. It's known for its lively ambiance, live music, and diverse international menu, offering a fun departure from traditional wine bar experiences.
picks.whatToOrder: A crisp, unoaked Chardonnay or a lighter red, to balance out the rich Polynesian flavors, along with their famous Crab Rangoon.
picks.insiderTip: Go on a night with live music for the full Trader Vic's experience. Their happy hour offers are also quite good for drinks.
picks.redditQuote: "Never thought I'd get a good glass of wine at Trader Vic's, but their list is actually decent for the vibe. It's super fun and a unique spot to hang out with friends for drinks."

faq.question: What kind of wine can I expect to find in Amman wine bars?
faq.answer: Amman's wine bars typically offer a diverse selection, ranging from popular international labels (French, Italian, Spanish, New World) to excellent local Jordanian wines. Many establishments proudly feature wines from Jordanian vineyards like Zumot and St. George, which are gaining international recognition for their quality.

faq.question: Are there dedicated wine bars in Amman, or are they usually part of restaurants?
faq.answer: While Amman has a growing appreciation for wine, dedicated wine-only bars are less common than in some Western cities. Most excellent wine selections are found within upscale restaurants, bistros, and hotel lounges that offer a strong bar component, ensuring you can enjoy a full meal or just drinks and small bites.

faq.question: What's the typical price range for a glass of wine in Amman?
faq.answer: The price for a glass of wine in Amman can vary widely depending on the venue and the wine itself. Generally, you can expect to pay between JOD 7-15 ($10-21 USD) for a standard glass of house or mid-range wine. Premium selections and higher-end venues will naturally command higher prices.

faq.question: Do Amman wine bars offer food pairings?
faq.answer: Yes, most wine bars and wine-focused restaurants in Amman offer excellent food pairings. You'll find everything from international tapas and cheese boards to full-course European or Mediterranean meals designed to complement their wine lists. Many places also feature local mezze that pair surprisingly well with certain wines.

faq.question: Is it customary to tip at wine bars in Amman?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Amman, especially at upscale establishments. A tip of 10-15% of the total bill is generally appreciated for good service. Some establishments might add a service charge, so it's always good to check your bill.

faq.question: Are there any local Jordanian wines worth trying?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Jordan has a nascent but rapidly developing wine industry. Wineries like Zumot (producing brands like Saint George) and Château Musar (though Lebanese, available in Jordan) offer excellent options. Look for their reds, often blends of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, and Syrah, and their crisp white wines which pair well with local cuisine.

methodology: Our selection of Amman's best wine bars is based on extensive research, analyzing online reviews, local recommendations, and menu offerings. We prioritize venues known for their diverse wine lists, knowledgeable staff, atmosphere, and complementary food options to ensure a truly memorable experience.
